name: just-the-browser
description: Remove AI features, telemetry data reporting, sponsored content, product integrations, and other annoyances from web browsers.
readme_summary: Just the Browser is a project that streamlines desktop web browsers by removing unwanted features like AI integrations, telemetry, and sponsored content. It aims to provide a clean, focused browsing experience using hidden enterprise settings and offers easy installation scripts and manual configuration guides for popular browsers.
key_features: Removes AI features, telemetry, sponsored content, and product integrations from web browsers.
Utilizes hidden enterprise settings for a streamlined experience.
Provides easy-to-use installation scripts for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Offers detailed manual installation guides for Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Firefox, and Brave.
Includes configuration files in various formats (.json, .reg, .mobileconfig).
Includes a static site generator for its documentation website.
primary_use_case: To strip down popular web browsers to their core functionality, removing distractions and privacy concerns for a cleaner, more focused user experience.
cover_image_prompt: A minimalist, pristine browser window, depicted as a clear glass dome, floating serenely in a clean, white digital space. Inside the dome, only the essential elements of a web page are visible, like a simple text document and a clear navigation bar. Surrounding the dome, like discarded clutter, are abstract, colorful shapes representing AI features, data streams, and intrusive advertisements, gently fading away. Subtle glowing lines connect the browser dome to a small, stylized 'JTB' logo. The overall aesthetic is clean, modern, and emphasizes clarity and focus, rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style with soft, ambient lighting.

name: fluidd
readme_summary: Fluidd is a free and open-source web interface designed for Klipper, a 3D printer firmware. It provides a responsive and customizable user interface for managing multiple 3D printers from various devices.
primary_use_case: Providing a user-friendly web interface to control and monitor Klipper-powered 3D printers.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled conductor standing at a podium, orchestrating a complex symphony of 3D printers. The conductor's baton, glowing with digital energy, directs streams of data (represented as musical notes and light trails) towards various printers, each depicted with intricate mechanical details. Small, stylized UI elements showing temperature graphs and print progress are subtly integrated into the scene. The background is a clean, modern workshop with soft, ambient lighting. The overall mood is one of precise control and harmonious operation. The image should be in a 3D isometric illustration style, emphasizing clarity and a sense of organized complexity, with the name 'Fluidd' subtly etched on the podium.

name: flowsint
description: A modern platform for visual, flexible, and extensible graph-based investigations. For cybersecurity analysts and investigators.
readme_summary: Flowsint is an open-source OSINT graph exploration tool designed for ethical investigation, transparency, and verification. It provides a modern platform for visual, flexible, and extensible graph-based investigations, primarily for cybersecurity analysts and investigators.
primary_use_case: Visualizing and exploring relationships in Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) data for cybersecurity investigations.
cover_image_prompt: A cybersecurity investigator stands at a holographic console, manipulating a complex, glowing network graph that represents interconnected digital entities. Streams of data flow from various sources (represented by abstract icons like social media logos, domain names, and IP addresses) into the graph, where they are visualized as nodes and edges. The investigator points to specific connections, causing them to highlight and reveal underlying details on a secondary screen displaying simplified code snippets and relationship metrics. The overall mood is one of focused discovery and clarity amidst complexity, rendered in a sleek, futuristic digital painting style with a dark, high-tech color palette and subtle glowing accents.

name: free-for-dev
description: A list of SaaS, PaaS and IaaS offerings that have free tiers of interest to devops and infradev
readme_summary: This repository is a curated list of Software as a Service (SaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) offerings that provide free tiers. It specifically targets infrastructure developers, DevOps practitioners, and system administrators, helping them discover valuable free resources for their work.
key_features: Curated list of free-tier SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS offerings
Focus on services useful for infrastructure developers (DevOps, SysAdmins)
Excludes self-hosted software, only includes as-a-service offerings
Requires free tier to be available for at least a year (if time-bucketed)
Considers security aspects, e.g., TLS not restricted to paid tiers
Community-driven through pull requests and contributions
primary_use_case: To help developers and DevOps practitioners discover and utilize free tiers of various cloud services and software offerings relevant to infrastructure development.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old librarian in a vast, organized library, meticulously sorting and shelving glowing books. Each book represents a different SaaS, PaaS, or IaaS service. The librarian is pointing to a specific shelf labeled 'Free Tiers for Devs', from which a beam of light emanates, illuminating a path for a curious developer character. Subtle digital particles representing data flow around the librarian and the books. The library has elements of a modern tech hub, with faint circuit board patterns on the walls. The overall mood is helpful and informative, with a clean, bright aesthetic. The image should be in a 3D isometric illustration style with rich details and vibrant colors, clearly showing the 'free-for.dev' repository name subtly integrated into a signpost.

name: CasaOS
description: CasaOS - A simple, easy-to-use, elegant open-source Personal Cloud system.
readme_summary: CasaOS is an open-source personal cloud operating system designed for ease of use and elegance. It simplifies the management of self-hosted applications and services, allowing users to easily deploy and manage Docker containers for a personalized home cloud experience.
primary_use_case: To provide a user-friendly interface for managing a personal cloud server, enabling easy deployment and management of self-hosted applications and services.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, stylized robot butler meticulously organizing and connecting various digital 'rooms' within a cozy, modern home. Each room represents a different self-hosted application (like a media server, file storage, or smart home hub), visually depicted by unique icons and subtle glowing connections. The robot is holding a tablet displaying the CasaOS logo and a simplified dashboard. The overall scene is warm, inviting, and uses a clean, 3D isometric illustration style with soft lighting, emphasizing ease of use and the seamless integration of digital services into a home environment.
